pr.title: Phase 1b: mail operations, ArzoieMail 6 and full-stack CI
pr.body:
This bundle delivers queue, route and rule administration through the native/REST/.NET panel, establishes the independent **ArzoieMail 6.0.0** release line, reconciles project documentation, and expands modern-stack CI on **every database backend**.

- Safe queue metadata/recipient inspection and guarded retry/removal; write-only TLS-protected routing credentials; scoped disabled rule drafts and separate checked activation. Stored/busy mail, parent IDs and protected roles are enforced natively. Rule persistence failures can leave disabled partial drafts requiring repair.
- VERSION is 6.0.0. Native/tool/installer metadata, API product metadata, schema-5714 UI label, release title format and product-identity regression follow the independent release policy. Existing schema/COM/service/assembly/installer identities and historical upgrade paths remain compatible. No public release is created.
- Documentation authority index, 46 capability records, inventories of all 89 maintained PHP sources and 54 desktop panes, complete delivery/migration gates and precise AI handoff/resumption rules. Static validation passed for 24 documents, 193 local links and complete capability/inventory ownership.
- Stable .NET 10 SDK policy, actual .NET/ASP.NET Core 10 runtime/x64/product checks, API publish/asset smoke, pipe impersonation checks, real REST/native persistence and roles/revocation/restart, actual production HTTPS/cookies/HSTS/Host/trust/name checks, HTTPS authentication through the real native service, and **published live browser tests without API mocks**. Retain fixture-based UI edge coverage. Upload redacted SDK/manifests/logs/screenshots per backend.

Current head: `28dd3df912fac9109260efe9f5571dc05b402d12`. All four database CI jobs passed the following **897 assertions per backend**, the fixture browser suite and the published live browser suite. Native/.NET/desktop and expanded test compilation passed. The exact tracked CI driver also passed in the disposable VM, including the selected product-version NUnit case, and the original VM checkpoint was restored:

| Layer | Assertions |
|---|---:|
| Deterministic DNS | 26 |
| HTTP/session contracts | 304 |
| Plaintext/forwarded-proto rejection | 2 |
| Native management/protocol effects | 402 |
| Actual .NET 10/runtime/product boundary | 7 |
| Pipe identity/impostor | 2 |
| Real REST/native/backend integration | 131 |
| Production HTTPS/cookies/Host/trust | 11 |
| Production HTTPS with real native service | 12 |
| **Total, excluding browser suites** | **897** |

Final-head NUnit results (no failures or warnings):

| Database | Total | Passed | Inconclusive | Skipped |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| SQL Server Compact | 1317 | 1207 | 34 | 76 |
| MySQL | 1317 | 1207 | 34 | 76 |
| PostgreSQL | 1317 | 1207 | 34 | 76 |
| SQL Server Express | 1317 | 1208 | 34 | 75 |

Release x64, workflow lint (actionlint/zizmor), GCC/Clang and CodeQL all passed on this head. Each backend uploaded its management evidence and NUnit results. CI installer publication also passed; this is not a public version-6 release.

Expanded CI correctly caught a fixture setup issue after runtime/TLS/pipe/native layers passed: the live REST host lacked its wwwroot because CI started at repository root. The driver now explicitly selects the published/source API content root and restores its caller's setting; the panel/asset assertion is retained. A VM rerun starts with the content-root variable unset to reproduce CI.

All runtime testing/previews are VM/CI-only. The original queue regression failed on the old VM binary and passed after the fix. Earlier CI exposed a browser request-history race, fixed with exact PATCH-response synchronization; an earlier PostgreSQL IP-range reachability failure passed on retry without code changes. New TLS fixtures use a Windows-backed generated test key, clear private PFX bytes, trust their CA only in the client policy, and require both chain/name rejection; no permissive certificate callback or trust-store installation.

[CI acceptance matrix](https://github.com/jassifx/ArzoieMail/blob/feature/webadmin-mail-operations/docs/ci-acceptance-matrix.md) explicitly tracks future tests for restricted IIS/service identity, controlled-clock expiry, actual installer/API provisioning, ACME/listener renewal, SpamAssassin engine, Defender lifecycle/EICAR/durable pressure, at least 10000 queued/in-flight capacity, PHP cutover and later phases. Current green functional checks must not be presented as those unimplemented capabilities. Queue DB paging, remaining parity, inherited-manual review and website publication remain unfinished.

PR remains unmerged. No next feature bundle, merge or release publication is authorized.

+## Status and evidence rules

+- **Merged** means the PR is merged into the development branch. Include its PR/merge reference.
+- **Implemented, verified, awaiting review** means code exists on an unmerged branch and named
+  checks passed on a specific commit. It does not mean released or installed for users.
+- **Partial** identifies delivered subfeatures and names the missing parts. A legacy desktop
+  or PHP capability does not establish that the replacement native/REST/panel exposes it.
+- **Planned / not started** is a requirement or design without accepted implementation.
+- **Unverified / decision required** is an unresolved question, not an assumed capability.
+- **Historical** records an earlier state. Older handoffs and test counts cannot override the
+  latest explicit record, or prove that a later revision passed.
+
+Source code establishes implemented behavior; tests and CI establish only the coverage they
+actually execute. If either disagrees with a document, record the discrepancy and correct the
+document or implementation. Do not use documentation to override an observed defect. GitHub
+is the live record for PR state and check execution; repository snapshots must give the exact
+revision/date and direct evidence links. A documentation commit cannot truthfully claim its

+   limitations. Keep local artifact paths optional; checked-in procedures and CI links must
+   let another agent work without ignored `out/` files.
+5. At submission, record the PR, branch and review gate. After CI, put final-head results in
+   the PR validation record. At merge/next authorized change, reconcile repository snapshots,
+   mark the merged item and clean only the authorized branches/artifacts.
+6. Preserve historical evidence with explicit labels. Keep secrets out of every document,

+
+Do not infer approval from a recommendation, green CI or elapsed time. Suggested next bundles
+remain proposals until the maintainer authorizes them. Do not merge or begin the next phase

+## Fixture boundaries and secret handling
+
+- Native and REST integration use temporary test identities and owned objects; COM is used only
+  by setup/cleanup. New-panel requests never use COM or direct SQL. Production SQL credentials
+  and mail data are not inputs to these suites.
+- Live HTTP integration runs on loopback Development hosting; production HTTPS behavior is
+  checked separately and also repeated with the real native channel. Published browser smoke
+  runs on loopback Development hosting. Neither establishes IIS provisioning or certificate
+  issuance/renewal. Those are separate acceptance gates.
+- HTTPS tests use a short-lived generated CA trusted only by their client chain policy. The
+  server test key is imported into a Windows user key context for Schannel and disposed; no
+  CA is added to a machine/user trust store. The normal client must reject the untrusted root,
+  and a trusted-root client must still reject a wrong hostname. Never replace this with an
+  always-true certificate callback.

+  machine-reboot deployment test. Fixture browsers cover more UI edge cases than the live

+  propagate failures. VM checkpoint restoration adds isolation; CI runner disposal is the final
+  safeguard, not a substitute for cleanup.

+# ArzoieMail release identity and version policy
+
+Decision: **2026-10-28, maintainer instruction**. ArzoieMail follows its own release trajectory.
+The next product release target is **ArzoieMail 6.0.0**, replacing the previous 5.8.0 target.
+The implementation and architecture have diverged; upstream hMailServer numbering no longer
+defines ArzoieMail's new releases. This is a development target, not a release announcement,
+publication instruction or claim that Phase 1b/other roadmap requirements are complete.
+
+## Version ownership and generated metadata
+
+| Value | Owner / format | Meaning |
+|---|---|---|
+| Next product target | Root [VERSION](../VERSION): `6.0.0` | Canonical three-part major.minor.patch release version |
+| Server-reported version | `6.0.0-B<build>` | Native service/COM/API status reports use the stamped product version and build |
+| Native PE and shipped desktop tool file/product versions | `6.0.0.<build>` | Windows resources, file properties and signing metadata |
+| Installer filename | `ArzoieMail-6.0.0-B<build>-x64.exe` | Product/version/build/architecture identity; existing installer AppId remains stable |
+| Installer display and version properties | `ArzoieMail 6.0.0-B<build>-x64`, numeric `6.0.0.<build>` | Installer/Windows version metadata; not the database schema version |
+| Release tag/title | `ArzoieMail-6.0.0-b<build>` / `ArzoieMail 6.0.0, build <build>` | Full three-part ArzoieMail version; manual release workflow creates a draft only when explicitly requested |
+| Management API product metadata | VersionPrefix read from `VERSION` | SDK-generated file/product metadata follows the product target; preview default build component is zero |
+| .NET assembly identity / COM typelib | Existing identity versions retained | Internal compatibility/binding contracts; a 1.x/5.x assembly identity is not a 5.x product-release target |
+| Database schema | `REQUIRED_DB_VERSION`, currently **5714** | Independent migration sequence; do not change it merely because product major becomes 6 |
+
+[Set-Version.ps1](../build/Set-Version.ps1) stamps the native header, shipped desktop-tool
+file/informational versions, generated legacy PHP version gate and installer setup metadata.
+Development metadata is committed at the target version with **build zero**. CI stamps a unique
+build number using its existing offset/run-number policy; the major-version change does not
+reset that sequence. The API reads its product prefix from VERSION and keeps assembly identity
+`1.0.0.0`; shipped desktop tools likewise retain existing assembly identities while their
+file/informational versions follow the stamp. Internal IDs are not marketing versions.
+
+The generated `WebAdmin/include_versioncheck.php` is ignored build output, not one of the 89
+maintained PHP source files. It remains necessary for legacy PHP compatibility until cutover;
+its generation/packaging must be retired with that application. Inventory checks exclude
+ignored outputs and include tracked/nonignored new sources.
+
+## Building and maintenance
+
+1. Change VERSION for a newly authorized product target. Update this policy, README, roadmap,
+   build examples, release metadata expectations and the latest handoff together.
+2. On the development host, generate development metadata without executing the product:
+
+   ```powershell
+   $releaseVersion = (Get-Content VERSION -Raw).Trim()
+   powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File build/Set-Version.ps1 $releaseVersion 0
+   ```
+
+3. Review generated diffs. Do not change assembly/COM identity, installer AppId, service names,
+   schema numbers or historical SQL filenames as a side effect. API metadata derives its prefix
+   directly from VERSION; production API build-number/signing integration belongs to hosting/
+   installer delivery and must be specified there rather than inferred from the preview.
+4. Compile on the host with service hooks disabled. Run executables, installer/upgrade tests,
+   previews and regressions only in the disposable VM or CI. Verify reported/PE versions,
+   displayed installer/tool versions, database-upgrade labels and existing-install compatibility.
+5. Require the four database jobs, other project CI gates and maintainer review. A successful
+   build/artifact upload does not publish a production release. Release creation/signing and
+   public publication need the maintainer's explicit release instruction and acceptance scope.
+
+Manual workflow version overrides remain available for controlled historical/reproduction
+builds; do not use a 5.8.x override as the new ArzoieMail release target. Future maintenance
+branches follow ArzoieMail releases, for example `6.0.0` or `6.0.1`, not an assumed upstream
+roadmap. Branch names and release tags must keep the workflow's supported syntax.
+
+## Compatibility and provenance
+
+- Preserve the identifiers listed in [AGENTS](../AGENTS.md): `hMailServer.exe`, service name,
+  COM ProgID/type library, INI, installer AppId, database tables, backup names, headers and

+- Preserve historical hMailServer release/schema mappings, SQL upgrade chains, original
+  authorship and AGPLv3/license notices. ArzoieMail remains derived from that code; independent
+  release ownership does not erase provenance or licensing obligations.
+- Schema 5714's current ArzoieMail display label is `ArzoieMail 6.0 (5714)`. The older

+- Keep older handoffs, test logs, manual examples and third-party dependency versions factual.

The maintainer approved a finite full-roadmap **ArzoieMail 6.0 integrated validation baseline** and resolved the Desktop documentation proposals question by question. This documentation-only PR records those decisions without claiming their implementation.

- Freeze all current Phase 0–6 deliverables; later scope changes require explicit approval. Add a canonical scope/checklist and breaking-change register.

- Require phase-level migration/recovery/security/load checks, then comprehensive frozen-baseline validation; independent review by responsibility/evidence; SQLite normal regression lanes plus retained Compact migration/recovery; supported-platform distinction; traceable builds, signed official production executables/setup, checksums and provenance.
- No development previews before feature completion; CI development-test installers remain allowed. Public releases still require explicit authorization. Bit-for-bit reproducibility remains a separate future goal.
- Reconcile merged #42 at `74eecc017` and tested head `28dd3df`: all four backends passed 1317 NUnit cases with zero failures/warnings, 897 assertions and both browser suites.
